newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals mixed early in light trade.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals mixed early in light trade.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were mixed after the first hour of trade, but volumes were light, and activity was slowed in the bullion market by May Day holidays in much of continental Europe and the Golden Week holidays in Japan, traders said.
* COMEX June gold was down 30 cents at $340.90 an ounce, after seeing a $341.50-340.50 early range.

* "There's not much in the way of speculative selling in the gold and the locals who went short on the open are buying it back as there's no follow though," North American Equity Services COMEX floor trader, John Geraghty said.
"There also some activity in the switchs with the back months holding up which is often a leading indicator," he said.
* In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted $339.10/60 early, compared to the London Thursday morning fix at $339.55 and the New York close Wednesday around $339.30/80.

* Physical offtake remained good in the Far East and through Dubai with refineries reporting increasing order books, but the U.S. dollar price was not responding, suggesting supply was coming from undisclosed European central bank activity, analysts said.

* In overnight news, Portugal's central bank said it carried out a number of gold swaps in late 1996 but had not sold any gold. The latest IMF data showed Portugal's gold reserves dropped by 1.06 million ounces in January to 14.4 million, but Portugal's central bank said this was accounted for by swaps.

* Renewed concerns about central bank gold sales, Australian producer hedging and renewed shorting by funds have driven gold prices down to test four year lows in the past week, but support has been found again around $340 an ounce, analysts noted.
* COMEX July silver was seen down opening unchanged to up 0.30 cent an ounce from the previous close at $4.693.
* Earlie this week, spot silver fixed at $4.6425, its lowest in two years, following the slide COMEX July silver to a new contract low at $4.630 on Monday.
* NYMEX July platinum was up 40 cents at $371.00 an ounce, while NYMEX June palladium was up 30 cents at $156.50.
* Significant lending into the PGM markets has reduced implied lease rates this week, allowing front month PGM futures to ease a little, analysts said.
* Rhodium prices remained around $275.00, after following other PGM's up in the past two months.
